kaps_punt: Suid-Afrika van 10 000 duisend jaar gelede: die mense van die Latere Steentydperk

items.bewering: Boeke en briewe vertel ons hoe mense lank gelede geleef het.
items.blok: Die tyd voordat mense geskryf het
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'prehistory' (britannica.com/dictionary/Prehistory); New World Encyclopedia, 'Prehistory': written records are the sources that separate history from prehistory.

items.bewering: Die voorgeskiedenis is die tyd voordat mense in 'n gebied begin skryf het. Uit daardie tyd is daar min of geen geskrewe bronne nie. Ons het dus ander leidrade nodig.
items.blok: Die tyd voordat mense geskryf het
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'prehistory': 'the period of time in the past before people could write'; New World Encyclopedia, 'Prehistory': the date marking the end of prehistory varies from region to region, which the lesson's 'in 'n gebied' captures.

items.bewering: Die drietydperkestelsel (Drietydperke-sisteem) deel die verlede in 'n Steentydperk, 'n Bronstydperk en 'n Ystertydperk in.
items.bron: Wikipedia and New World Encyclopedia, 'Christian Jürgensen Thomsen' / 'Three-age system'; Buckinghamshire Council Heritage Portal, 'Three Age System': Thomsen (1836) classified finds as stone, bronze and iron and argued these were three successive ages.

items.bewering: Elke naam sê waarvan baie gereedskap in daardie tyd gemaak is.
items.bron: Three-age system (Wikipedia; Buckinghamshire Heritage Portal): the system classifies prehistory by the material used for tools and cutting implements. 'Baie' correctly avoids claiming all tools.

items.bewering: In Suider-Afrika was daar egter nie 'n aparte Bronstydperk nie.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Stone Age: Southern Africa' (search extract; page returned 403 on direct fetch): no evidence of a Copper or Bronze Age in Africa outside the Sudan; Journal of African History (Cambridge), 'The Southern Rhodesian Iron Age': no copper- or bronze-using stage between the stone- and iron-using phases; Cambridge, African Archaeology: in most of Africa south of the equator farming and iron-working began at about the same time.

items.bewering: Die Steentydperk het sy naam gekry omdat baie gereedskap toe van klip gemaak is.
items.bron: Thomsen's Guide (via Wikipedia 'Three-age system'): the Stone Age as the period when weapons and tools were made of stone, wood, bone or similar materials and metals were little known.

items.bewering: Klip bly ook langer behoue as die hout, been en vel wat mense gebruik het.
items.bron: LibreTexts, 'Archaeology: It's More Than Digging in the Dirt', 5.01 Deterioration and Decomposition: stone is inherently more durable than organic materials, which decay biologically; Sapiens, 'gender archaeology': the record of tool use is skewed toward the hardier stone.

items.bewering: Van oudste na jongste is die drie dele die Vroeë Steentydperk, die Middelsteentydperk en die Later Steentydperk.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': ESA from about 2.6 million years ago, then the MSA, then the LSA from about 25 000 years ago; Villa et al., 'Border Cave and the beginning of the Later Stone Age in South Africa' (PNAS, via USF Digital Commons): MSA to LSA at about 44-42 ka. The order is right. Note for a person, not a finding: Afrikaans general reference (af.wikipedia 'Steentydperk') uses 'Vroeë Steentydperk' for the European Palaeolithic and the Mesolitikum for the middle phase, so the Afrikaans names can carry the European sense elsewhere; the lesson uses them in the South African ESA/MSA/LSA sense, and its own definitions are true in that sense.

items.bewering: In Suid-Afrika het die Vroeë Steentydperk sowat twee miljoen jaar gelede begin.
items.bron: Granger, Gibbon, Kuman et al. 2015, 'New cosmogenic burial ages for Sterkfontein Member 2 Australopithecus and Member 5 Oldowan', Nature 522: 85-88 (abstract via USF Digital Commons): earliest Sterkfontein stone tools 2.18 ± 0.21 million years, similar to Swartkrans and Wonderwerk; Times Live, 21 April 2015, 'Our ancestors used knives two million years ago'. The global ESA starts about 2.6 million years ago (Ethiopia; SAHO), so the lesson's 'In Suid-Afrika' qualifier is necessary and present.

items.bewering: Stel jou 'n pad van 200 meter voor wat van twee miljoen jaar gelede tot vandag strek. Die laaste 10 000 jaar is dan net die laaste meter van die pad.
items.bron: Arithmetic: 2 000 000 years / 200 m = 10 000 years per metre, so the last 10 000 years is exactly the last metre. Mapping checked: a linear scale model of time, start point tied to the ESA start in South Africa (about 2 million years, Granger et al. 2015) and end point today. Reasoning further from it (older is further back along the road, recent periods are short stretches) leads nowhere false.

items.bewering: Hierdie kwartaal gaan oor die mense van die laaste 10 000 jaar van die Later Steentydperk.
items.bron: The phrasing implies the LSA is longer than 10 000 years, which is right: SAHO 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' puts the LSA start at about 25 000 years ago and Villa et al. (Border Cave, PNAS) at about 44-42 ka. SAHO 'The San' article also treats the last 10 000 years of the LSA as the period whose sites link directly to the San.

items.bewering: Daar was jagter-versamelaars, die voorouers van die San, en later ook herders.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': LSA hunter-gatherers 'in southern Africa ... were the ancestors of the San'; SAHO, 'The San': skeletons from the last 10 000 years resemble recent San, and Khoikhoi herders brought sheep and cattle within the last 2 000 years; Oakhurst ancient DNA (Nature Ecology & Evolution 2024, s41559-024-02532-3): genetic continuity with living San over about 10 000 years.

items.bewering: Jagter-versamelaars het wilde diere gejag en veldkos versamel.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' and 'The San'; Library of Congress Country Studies, South Africa: San lived by gathering edible plants, berries and shellfish, by hunting game, and by fishing.

items.bewering: Hulle het nog lank ná die koms van boere met yster op hul eie manier bly leef.
items.bron: SAHO, 'The San': Iron Age farmers settled the summer-rainfall regions within the last 1 800 years and lived alongside hunter-gatherers; /Xam hunter-gatherers survived in the Northern Cape into the 19th century, and several thousand Kalahari people were still hunting large game with poisoned arrows in the 1950s.

items.bewering: voorgeskiedenis: Die tyd voordat mense in 'n gebied begin skryf het.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'prehistory'; New World Encyclopedia, 'Prehistory' (end date varies by region). True when read alone.

items.bewering: drietydperkestelsel: 'n Indeling van die verlede in 'n Steen-, Brons- en Ystertydperk.
items.bron: Three-age system (Wikipedia; Buckinghamshire Heritage Portal; New World Encyclopedia, 'Christian Jürgensen Thomsen').

items.bewering: brons: 'n Metaal wat mense maak deur koper en tin saam te smelt.
items.bron: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Bronze': an alloy traditionally made of copper and tin (modern bronze about 88% copper, 12% tin); 1911 Britannica: an alloy of copper and tin in variable proportions. An alloy is a metal, so 'n Metaal' holds.

items.bewering: Bronstydperk: Die tyd toe baie gereedskap van brons gemaak is.
items.bron: Thomsen's Guide (via Wikipedia 'Three-age system'): the Bronze Age as the time of copper or bronze weapons and cutting tools. The entry read alone does not say where; the study block's statement that Southern Africa had no separate Bronze Age keeps the whole lesson true.

items.bewering: Ystertydperk: 'n Naam wat argeoloë gebruik vir die tyd nadat mense gereedskap van yster begin maak het.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': metalworking as a new technology that archaeologists label the Iron Age; Thomsen (Wikipedia 'Three-age system'): the Iron Age as the period when iron replaced bronze for suitable uses.

items.bewering: Steentydperk: Die lang tyd toe mense baie van hul gereedskap van klip gemaak het.
items.bron: Thomsen's Guide (via Wikipedia 'Three-age system'); SAHO 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' (from about 2.6 million years ago, so 'lang' is right).

items.bewering: Vroeë Steentydperk: Die oudste van die drie dele van die Steentydperk.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': ESA first, from about 2.6 million years ago, ending about 400 000-250 000 years ago.

items.bewering: Middelsteentydperk: Die middelste van die drie dele van die Steentydperk.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa'; Villa et al., Border Cave (PNAS): MSA between ESA and LSA, ending about 44-42 ka at Border Cave. True also if a reader takes the term in its European (Mesolithic) sense, which is likewise the middle of three parts.

items.bewering: Later Steentydperk: Die jongste van die drie dele van die Steentydperk.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': the LSA follows the MSA and is the last of the three.

items.bewering: jagter-versamelaar: Iemand wat kos kry deur wilde diere te jag en veldkos te versamel.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' and 'The San'; Library of Congress Country Studies, South Africa.

items.bewering: herder: Iemand wat vee aanhou en oppas, soos beeste en skape.
items.bron: SAHO, 'The San': Khoikhoi herders brought sheep and cattle into South Africa within the last 2 000 years. The examples match the herders this lesson introduces.

opsomming: Every claim checked out, including the four superlatives, the 2-million-year South African start date (Sterkfontein, 2.18 ± 0.21 million years) and the road analogy (exactly 10 000 years per metre); two things for a person that are not fact findings: the lesson's metadata line for the CAPS heading reads '10 000 duisend jaar', and the Afrikaans period names can carry the European sense in general reference works, though the lesson uses them correctly in the South African sense.
